retrieval.name: keyword-all-words
retrieval.config: websearch_to_tsquery (every word must match) OR last-word prefix; index holds title + tags (weight A) and first ~240 chars of each note (weight B)
retrieval.notes: Rank of the expected note in the top k, or null if missed. Every hit came from the last-word prefix fallback; no full question matched any note.

retrieval.name: keyword-any-word
retrieval.config: match="any": plainto_tsquery with & swapped for | (any word matches, more words rank higher), no prefix; same index as above. Run through search() directly, the path the assistant uses
retrieval.notes: q006 and q008 miss on vocabulary (question and note use different words). q005's answer is past the indexed excerpt. q001 ranks 4th behind two Google Tasks titled 'Personal OS': common words outranking the real answer. The q010 trap now returns 5 unrelated F1 events instead of nothing.

retrieval.name: keyword-any-word-full-body
retrieval.config: match="any" as above; notes' tsvector built from the full body (title+tags weight A, body weight B), excerpt still the only stored text; ts_rank with no length normalization (normalizations 1 and 2 tested first: same recall with worse MRR, and 0/9)
retrieval.notes: q005 found now that its answer is searchable. Long notes (Plan, LEARNING, backlog) crowd the top 3 and push q004 and q009 down: the case for chunking. q006 still misses on vocabulary. q008 is beaten by ADR-010, which arguably also answers it (label question). The q010 trap now returns backlog/Plan_2/Plan: near-topic text, harder for the model to refuse than the F1 events were.

retrieval.name: keyword-any-word-full-body-30q
retrieval.config: same search as keyword-any-word-full-body; dataset grown from 10 to 30 questions (25 answerable, 5 traps). First run of evals/run_retrieval.py, matching on (source, provider_id)
